title: Use one alpha interval while paying rate- and width-dependent constants
statement: For fixed finite phases and one unbounded count, use residual r=n+beta_j and fixed rational 0<alpha<1/2. The nonneutral lifted component proof assigns edge tilt r^(alpha delta)2^|delta|; an upward edge returns along its first downward path with burden r^[-(1-2alpha)delta]. It drops vanishing downward Dirichlet terms while retaining endpoint sinks. Every component with a nonzero residual increment is eventually Hurwitz; all-delta-zero components are separate. v=(-G^T)^(-1)1 yields mu=Gamma(r+1)^(-alpha)v and u=(-G)^(-1)1 yields primal Gamma(r+1)^alpha u. Fixed-shift ratios are 1+O(1/r). The alpha interval is independent of phase count/rates/orders, but constants and thresholds are not. Rational rates allow exact rational-function acquisition in r^(1/q); conceptual positive real rates do not automatically supply that algorithm.
